Thailand Telecoms Sector Hit by Nationwide Walkout as Workers Demand Higher Wages

A nationwide walkout of telecommunications workers in Thailand entered its second day on Thursday, disrupting operations at network control centres and call centres of major telecoms firms. The strike, organized by the Thai Telecommunications Union (TTU), is the largest such action in the industry in over a decade and has seen participation from thousands of employees across the country.

Workers from key operators, including SiamTel Communications and Lotus Mobile Networks, have joined the walkout, demanding a 12% wage increase and improved overtime pay. According to the TTU, more than 7,500 staff across 21 sites have stopped work, affecting maintenance schedules, technical support, and some customer service functions.

“We are committed to negotiating a fair deal for our members, who have not seen a significant pay rise in six years,” said TTU President Apichai Srisuwan. “The companies’ current offer falls far short of what is needed to keep pace with the cost of living.”

Industry analysts say the walkout has led to delays in scheduled upgrades, routine maintenance, and customer support responses at affected sites. “Firms are relying on management and a limited number of non-union staff to maintain essential operations, but the impact is being felt,” said Chanin Boonma, an industry consultant at AsiaTel Insights.

A spokesperson for Lotus Mobile Networks stated, “We are working to minimize disruption for our clients and hope to reach a resolution with our employees as soon as possible.”

The TTU has indicated that the strike will continue until a new agreement is reached. Negotiations between unions and management are ongoing.
